newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, seen up on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, seen up on Friday.

text.p: Polish shares rebounded on Thursday after a two-session dip and analysts saw the main market, currently at 15,208.8 points, rising again on Friday after having fallen from about 16,500 points since mid-June.

"It seems we've reached a bottom from which we have a chance to build, though until the elections I don't see potential for there to be sudden dynamic growth," said Sebastian Buczek, an analyst at ING BSK Asset Management.
Buczek said current rises could reach 16,000 points. Poland's parliamentary elections are due on September 21.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.9 percent to 15,208.2 points and turnover inched up one percent to 194.4 million zlotys ($58.9 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 68 to 23 with 18 stocks flat.
Analysts said an uptrend was also possible next week as the offering of copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA ends on Friday.
On Saturday shares in the firm's domestic large investor non-preferred tranche are to be allotted at a special bourse session from the minimum price 19.5 zlotys ($5.9).
Analysts said this week's rises by newcomer Bank Handlowy, up 1.3 percent on Monday in lower 56.2-million-zloty ($17 million) trade, suggested large investors were buying.
They said Handlowy should extend gains on Friday.

Analysts said loss leader Polfa Kutno, down seven percent in light trade, was hurt by the news it might have tax arrears of 7.1 million zlotys ($2.2 million) which the drug maker said it would contest at a higher local tax authority.
